concepts.name: Product verification
concepts.description: Checks a realized product against its requirements or specifications.

concepts.name: Product validation
concepts.description: Checks that the product meets stakeholder expectations in its intended environment.

concepts.name: Requirements and specifications
concepts.description: Documented conditions against which product verification provides evidence.

concepts.name: Stakeholder expectations
concepts.description: Expectations used to assess whether the realized product is suitable for its users.

concepts.name: Intended environment
concepts.description: The environment in which users are expected to use the system.

concepts.name: End-to-end testing
concepts.description: Testing across elements and interfaces to demonstrate system-level compatibility and functionality.

concepts.name: Interface compatibility
concepts.description: Compatibility among system elements and external enabling systems.

concepts.name: Technical risk management
concepts.description: Identifies, assesses, mitigates, and monitors technical risks.

concepts.name: Technical risk
concepts.description: Potential future performance shortfall related to safety, technical performance, cost, or schedule.

concepts.name: Risk mitigation
concepts.description: Actions selected to reduce or manage a risk and its consequences.

passages.title: Product verification
passages.text: Product verification proves that an end product (whether built, coded, bought, or reused) for any element within the system structure conforms to its requirements or specifications.

passages.title: Verification and validation objectives
passages.text: The Product Verification Process answers the critical question, “Was the end product realized right?”

passages.title: Product validation
passages.text: Validation proves whether “the right product was done.” Validation is performed for the benefit of the customers and users to ensure that the system functions in the expected manner when placed in the intended environment. This is achieved by examining the products of the system at every level of the product structure and comparing them to the stakeholder expectations for that level.

passages.title: End-to-end testing
passages.text: The purpose of end-to-end testing is to demonstrate interface compatibility and desired total functionality among different elements of a mission system, between the system of interest and external enabling systems, and within a system as a whole.

passages.title: End-to-end testing scope
passages.text: End-to-end tests may be performed as part of investigative engineering tests, verification testing, or validation testing.

passages.title: Technical risk
passages.text: Risk is the potential for performance shortfalls, which may be realized in the future, with respect to achieving explicitly established and stated performance requirements. The shortfalls may relate to safety, technical performance, cost, or schedule.

passages.title: Identify technical risks
passages.text: On a continuing basis, the technical team will identify technical risks including their source, analyze the potential consequence and likelihood of the risks occurring, and prepare clear risk statements for entry into the program/project risk management system.

passages.title: Risk mitigation and monitoring
passages.text: This includes selecting the risks that will be mitigated and more closely monitored, identifying the risk level or threshold that will trigger a risk mitigation action plan.
